toolsAdded.name: schedule_nudge
toolsAdded.description: Schedule a message you will deliver to this conversation later on your own, such as a reminder. Give either `at` or `in_minutes`. Add `every_minutes` to repeat it.

message.description: What to say or remind about when it fires.

at.description: Local time, like 2026-10-13T14:30, in the time zone of whoever asked: theirs if the members section names one, else Europe/Oslo.

every_minutes.description: Repeat this often, in minutes; at least 1.

toolsAdded.name: list_nudges
toolsAdded.description: List the nudges scheduled in this conversation, soonest first.

toolsAdded.name: cancel_nudge
toolsAdded.description: Cancel a scheduled nudge of this conversation by its id.

toolsAdded.name: remember
toolsAdded.description: Remember a lasting fact for this conversation, such as a preference, a plan or a name. You will see it in every later turn here, also after older messages are summarized. Only the people in this conversation can see it. One short fact per call. In someone's personal conversation, set `everywhere` for a fact about them that matters wherever they are: it goes in their own memory, which they can choose to share with all their conversations.

everywhere.description: Only in a personal conversation. Default false.

toolsAdded.name: forget
toolsAdded.description: Forget a fact this conversation remembers, by its id (like m3). Someone's own facts (like p2) can be forgotten only in their personal conversation.

toolsAdded.name: show_ui
toolsAdded.description: Show a card in the chat with blocks (heading, markdown text, key-value pairs, a list, a table, an image attachment by id, a divider, a map, a chart, stats, progress bars, a timeline), fields to fill in and up to 6 buttons. Use it when people pick between a few options, fill in several values, or compare things side by side; not for plain answers, which stay text. A `map` shows places by lat/lon with a label each, and a `path` for a route. A `chart` is `bar` (comparing amounts), `line` or `area` (change over time) or `pie` (parts of one whole, one series, up to 8 slices); give a value per label in each series, and keep two measures of different scale in two charts. `stats` is a few headline numbers with what changed; `progress` is how far along things are; `timeline` is steps in order. An `event` is something for a calendar (start and end as a day, or a time with its offset such as 2026-11-03T18:00+01:00), which people can add to theirs. A `diagram` is boxes (`nodes`) joined by arrows (`edges`), laid out for you. Fields may also be a `date` (YYYY-MM-DD), a `time` (HH:MM), `choices` (any of its options, a list) or a `range` (a number from `min` to `max` on a slider). A button with a `url` opens that page after asking, and doesn't come back to you. Nobody has to press: they may also just write. A press comes back as a message such as `Pressed "Book" on "Times"` with a line per field; answer it as you would that message. Buttons work once unless `once` is false. `who: "asker"` lets only who you answer press. Fields' values reach you, so never ask for passwords or keys with them. Don't repeat the card's content in your text.

toolsAdded.name: update_ui
toolsAdded.description: Show a card you showed earlier with `show_ui` again, changed: the card in the chat becomes this one, such as the next step of a delivery, a new total, or a list with an item ticked off. `call_id` is that show_ui call's id. Give the whole card, not just what changed. Its buttons work again. Use it to keep one card current instead of showing a new one each time; show a new card for something new.

call_id.description: The id of the show_ui call that showed the card.
